FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not evaluate fixes in a real sandboxed project context. It copies only the target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file. Any fix whose correctness depends on sibling modules, package-relative imports, or neighboring files will be assessed against an incomplete environment. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` never copies the package tree or preserves the original relative path; it only writes one basename into `tmpdir` and then invokes tool runners on that standalone file.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” capability can return silently wrong verdicts for realistic fixes. A fix that is actually safe in the real codebase can be marked HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE because imports fail in the stripped sandbox; a fix that breaks cross-file interfaces can be marked SAFE because only the edited file is checked. This crosses the endocrine→immune interface directly: `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when `evaluate_fixes()` returns SAFE or NEUTRAL, so a false SAFE here can close bugs prematurely in NK’s bug-closed gate, while a false HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE can prevent valid fixes from ever being verified.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — in `evaluate_fix()`, copy the full relevant source tree into the temp directory while preserving relative paths, patch the target file in place inside that copied tree, and run pyright/ruff/bandit/test commands from the sandbox root against the sandbox-relative target path rather than against a lone basename file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` is not actually bound to the patched file. The code runs `test_cmd` in `cwd=tmpdir`, but it does not rewrite test command paths or PYTHONPATH to point at the sandboxed project copy. In the current implementation, only a single patched file exists in `tmpdir`; any command like the one used by `immune_agents` (`["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`) refers to paths that do not exist under that temp directory, or imports the real project from elsewhere on `sys.path` instead of the patched copy. Evidence: `evaluate_fix()` passes `test_cmd` unchanged to `_run_tool(..., cwd=tmpdir)`, with no path remapping and no environment override.
FOLLOW: This makes the “tests_passed” signal mechanically unreliable. Tests may fail for the wrong reason (missing test paths in tempdir), or pass against unpatched source if Python resolves imports from the real repository. The downstream effect is fix misclassification in `_compute_fix_verdict()`, which then feeds immune stage 4 verification and can incorrectly set or withhold `verified=True` on findings. That directly affects reviewer-visible outputs and bug lifecycle state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — after copying the relevant project tree into the temp directory, rewrite or construct the test command to target sandbox-relative paths and run it with an environment that puts the sandbox root first on `PYTHONPATH` so tests execute against the patched copy only.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong file by substring match. It extracts `*.py` fragments from `finding.description + " " + finding.proposed_fix` and returns the first `source_path` where `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. The `match in sp_path` clause is unsafe: a short or generic fragment can match multiple unrelated paths, and the first list order wins. Evidence: for any source list containing overlapping names/directories, e.g. `bench/endocrine.py` and another path containing `endocrine.py` as a substring or embedded fragment, the function can resolve to the wrong target without checking uniqueness.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can patch and analyze the wrong file while still producing a normal-looking result. That contaminates pre/post counts, verdicts, and `original_file`, making SAFE/HARMFUL decisions silently wrong. Downstream, immune stage 4 may verify the wrong bug fix and mark the actual finding as `verified=True`, which then propagates into NK dedup/bug-closed behavior and the registry summary shown to models.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — restrict resolution to exact normalized path matches or unique basename/suffix matches only; if multiple `source_paths` match a cited fragment, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of guessing.
VERIFIED: TRUE

EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` also misreports tool availability on timeout, not just missing binaries. `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")`; the runners generally return `[]` without surfacing that status, so `scan_health()` sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. This makes timed-out scans look healthy and undermines reviewer trust in health-scan coverage.

EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is not only a parsing-loss issue; it also poisons system-level status. Because runners collapse timeout to `[]`, `scan_health()` logs the tool as available and healthy, so a completely skipped analyzer becomes indistinguishable from “no diagnostics found.” That is a HIGH consequence in the endocrine→brain health signal path.

EXTEND C0005 | The dead/partial feature issue also covers the fix-evaluation claim. The module docstring promises “sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source),” but the current implementation is only file-local sandboxing and does not preserve project context for imports/tests. The feature fires, but not correctly enough to support its advertised role as the immune pipeline’s fix verifier.
